content.comment_body: Hello, When I press the button, the light does not turn on. I have attached a video: [url]
Are you using backlight flags in your program? If you are, the automatic backlight activation feature will be disabled.
Yes, I use the red indicator light to show errors. I have attached an image of the code. Should I use M25 instead of M30?
No, the issue is that when these special flags are used, the automatic activation by button press is disabled.

There is not a straightforward solution. Option 1: Do not use any special flags for the backlight. Option 2: In your program, you can check for cursor key presses and combine these. This will trigger the marker for the white background lighting with a delay before switching off. However, this means you need to press the cursor key along with the ESC key (ESC + cursor key). [IMAGE]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are finding it confusing to activate the LCD backlight on the [product_name] when special backlight flags are used in their programming. Setting these flags disables the automatic function, and users are looking for solutions or workarounds. Although possible using custom programming logic, the lack of straightforward interface guidance makes the product less intuitive.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect that pressing a button on the [product_name] should activate the LCD backlight, regardless of the use of special backlight programming flags.
